factual_and_methodological.summary: Primary BlackRock evidence confirms US$15.3tn AUM at 30 Jun 2026, US$868bn twelve-month net inflows, the Voting Choice subsets (US$8.79tn index equity, US$3.96tn eligible, US$923bn actively exercising), and the delegated nature of stewardship. The dossier consistently separates client AUM, beneficial ownership, proxy authority and operational corporate control.

editorial_publication_readiness.opening: Direct mechanism-led opening; no generic sophistication claims or product-process narration.
editorial_publication_readiness.headings: Headings advance the actor-specific mechanism, constraints, contrary evidence and revision conditions.
editorial_publication_readiness.language_localization: EN and PT-BR are semantically aligned; PT-BR technical prose was localized before approval.
editorial_publication_readiness.cohesion: Argument moves from rights/capability through transmission, constraints and evidence that would revise the assessment.
editorial_publication_readiness.template_meta_qa: No prompt, QA-process, schema, renderer or roadmap leakage detected.

contextual_depth.summary: The dossier distinguishes legal rights, operating capability, transmission, substitutability and institutional constraints rather than relying on scale or reputation.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: At least two analytical tables, one quantitative chart, one causal flow and one mind map in both locales.
visual_evidence_readiness.limitations: Visuals encode sourced quantities or mechanisms defended in prose and are not combined into a synthetic power score.

contrary_evidence: Voting Choice demonstrates that proxy authority is divisible and can migrate back toward client-selected policies even while AUM rises.
Asset owners can switch mandates, redeem many products, use competing managers or internalise investment functions; aggregate AUM is therefore not a monopoly measure.
limitations: Technology-services growth establishes a material commercial channel but does not by itself prove low switching costs or lock-in.
Governance effects depend on mandate, authorisation, proposal type and the votes of other shareholders.
notes: Dedicated single-actor Strategic Actors dossier. Primary-source factual core, controlled taxonomy, bilingual parity and visual evidence reviewed; no public bundle for this ID at approval time.

en.title: BlackRock: structural reach through delegated capital, voting authority and financial infrastructure
en.deck: BlackRock's US$15.3 trillion AUM is not ownership. Its structural relevance comes from delegated portfolio implementation, shareholder rights where clients authorize them, and investment infrastructure—with explicit limits from mandates, client choice and competition.
en.regime: Large-scale asset management combines persistent delegated intermediation with divisible shareholder-voting authority.
en.key_risk: Treating client AUM, proxy voting and beneficial ownership as equivalent overstates direct corporate control.

pt-BR.title: BlackRock: alcance estrutural por capital delegado, autoridade de voto e infraestrutura financeira
pt-BR.deck: Os US$ 15,3 trilhões em AUM da BlackRock não são propriedade da gestora. Sua relevância vem da implementação de mandatos, de direitos acionários quando autorizados pelos clientes e de infraestrutura de investimento, com limites explícitos de mandato, escolha do cliente e concorrência.
pt-BR.regime: Gestão de ativos em grande escala combina intermediação delegada persistente com autoridade de voto acionário divisível.
pt-BR.key_risk: Tratar AUM de clientes, voto por procuração e propriedade beneficiária como equivalentes exagera o controle corporativo direto.
